title: Vithu mauli: God as mother
hook: a man with a gray beard, soaked from the rain, calls the god he's walking to 'mother'
carry: God is mother, so the walkers are family
tomorrow: who rides in a palanquin with no one inside?

segments.voice: Yesterday, serving your parents is serving God: Pundalik's brick, and a god who waits, hands on hips.

A man with a gray beard, soaked from the rain, stops at the side of the road to tie his sandal. When he stands up again, he lifts his arms and calls out, not to a friend, but to the god at the end of the road. And the word he uses is mother. Vithu mauli. Vitthal, mother. Nobody around him finds that strange. The god he's walking toward is shown as a man standing on a brick, and here is an old man calling him mother. Today, the names Varkaris give their god, and why one of them is mother.
screen: `A GRAY BEARD IN THE RAIN.` → `HE CALLS OUT: MOTHER.` → `VITHU MAULI.`

segments.voice: The god of Pandharpur has more than one name, and each is a different way of coming close. Vitthal is the name on the temple. Vithoba adds a touch of affection, the way a family turns a name into a nickname. Pandurang is another, and Varkaris hear in all of them the same god, a form of Krishna, standing on his brick. Then there's mauli. In Marathi it's a tender word for mother, and Varkari songs use it for Vitthal. Why mother, for a god shown as a man? Because you don't need to be worthy to run to a mother. You don't need the right words or the right clothes. You come tired, wet and hungry, and she takes you in. In songs tradition gives to Namdev and Tukaram, the singer calls out to Vitthal this way, as a child calls a mother, without ceremony. And the word doesn't stop with God. Varkaris call Jnaneshwar mauli too, and the cry Jnanoba Mauli rises from the road. On the road, pilgrims call one another mauli. A stranger offering you tea is mauli. The person whose feet you bow to is mauli. So one tender word runs from the god, to the saint, to the person walking next to you. That's the heart of bhakti: you come close to God the way a child comes to a mother, and if the god at the end of the road is a mother, then the people on the road with you are family.
screen: `VITTHAL, VITHOBA, PANDURANG` · `MAULI: MOTHER` · `RUN TO HIM LIKE A CHILD` · `THE STRANGER BESIDE YOU, MAULI`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who took you in when you came to them tired: a parent, a grandparent, a friend, a teacher. Remember what it felt like to arrive without needing the right words, and let that same warmth widen to one stranger you saw today. If you pray, you can call God by whatever tender name your own tradition gives.
Maharashtra's Varkari. The tradition that calls its god Vithu mauli, mother, and calls the pilgrim next to it mauli too. Today's word.
Hold on to it: God is mother, so the walkers are family. One word, mauli, turns the whole road into kin. See you tomorrow.
